meta.name: Slow Walks and Mindful Observation
meta.author: OUTSIDE//OS Core Team & Hacktoberfest Contributors
meta.description: De-accelerate screen fatigue through sensory grounding, auditory surveying, and micro-climatic awareness.
safety_guidelines: Select quiet paths with minimal vehicular interference.
Never close your eyes while stepping across curbs or uneven grades.
Stay hydrated and dress appropriately for current wind chill or heat.

quests.title: The Decibel Horizon
quests.objective: Catalog the layering of sounds in your surroundings from immediate breath to distant horizons.
quests.suitability_reason: Relieves digital cognitive overload through auditory grounding in 15 quiet minutes.

steps.instruction: Find a bench, low stone, or open grassy space and sit comfortably.
steps.detail: Rest your hands palms-up on your thighs and soften your gaze toward the ground.

steps.instruction: Listen for sounds within arms reach: your clothing rustling, your breathing, a nearby twig.
steps.detail: Spend one minute focused purely on the immediate sound circle.

steps.instruction: Expand your awareness to the middle distance: swaying treetops, footfalls, bird calls.
steps.detail: Count how many organic vs mechanical noises you distinguish.

steps.instruction: Reach for the farthest sonic horizon: distant trains, highway hum, wind gusts over ridgelines.
steps.detail: Notice how the auditory field never remains truly silent.

checklist: Identified the quietest sound in your immediate perimeter
Distinguished at least one natural bird or insect frequency
Pinpointed a sound originating from beyond your visual horizon
Remained stationary for at least 7 minutes without checking notifications
quests.bonus_challenge: Notice how your shoulders drop and neck tension eases as you listen.
quests.safe_alternative: Sit near an open window indoors and close your eyes for 5 minutes cataloging sounds.
quests.completion_criteria: Spend 10 minutes in sustained auditory awareness.
quests.reflection_question: Which distant sound carried the furthest, and did it feel calming or distracting?
safety_notes: Maintain baseline awareness of public thoroughfares.
Choose daylight hours and well-populated public spaces.

quests.title: Thermal Micro-Climates
quests.objective: Detect three distinct changes in ambient temperature and air currents along a 200-meter route.
quests.suitability_reason: Engages physical skin sensation to re-connect neural pathways to outdoor reality.

steps.instruction: Walk at half-speed along your chosen path with hands out of your pockets.
steps.detail: Expose the skin on your cheeks and hands to the ambient air.

steps.instruction: Step from direct sunlight into deep shade under an awning or tree canopy.
steps.detail: Notice the immediate sensory drop in radiant warmth.

steps.instruction: Locate a corridor where air moves faster (between buildings or trees).
steps.detail: Determine the direction the air current is moving by feeling it against your temples.

checklist: Felt temperature contrast between direct sun and shade
Determined wind direction without looking at a weather app
Walked at a pace slower than ordinary pedestrian traffic
quests.bonus_challenge: Touch a sun-warmed stone or wooden post and feel the thermal mass stored within it.
quests.safe_alternative: Open two opposite windows in your home and observe the cross-breeze across your face.
quests.completion_criteria: Notice and record two distinct micro-climatic zones.
quests.reflection_question: How did your physical body respond to moving between sun, wind, and shade?
safety_notes: In cold weather, avoid hypothermia by dressing in layers.
In hot weather, seek shade and avoid midday peak UV exposure.
